title: SessionEnd's shared 1.5s budget
summary: All Claude Code SessionEnd hooks share one 1.5-second budget, not 1.5s each. Anything slower is cancelled with its output discarded. Setting a per-hook `timeout` raises the shared budget (up to 60s) but does not extend hooks that have no `timeout` of their own, and a plugin's own hook timeouts never raise the budget at all.

body.problem: Your SessionEnd cleanup hook — flushing a log, uploading session stats, killing a sidecar — works when you run the script by hand but silently does nothing on `/clear` or exit. It is being cancelled: Claude Code gives SessionEnd hooks a default 1.5-second budget, and that budget is shared across every SessionEnd hook of every type rather than granted per hook. A cancelled hook's output is discarded, and SessionEnd hooks have no decision control, so nothing in the transcript tells you the work was dropped.
steps: Decide the real wall-clock cost of the cleanup. If it can exceed ~1.5s total across all your SessionEnd hooks, you must raise the budget explicitly.

Option A - per-hook timeout: add `"timeout": <seconds>` to that hook's entry in a settings file. The shared budget rises to match the highest per-hook `timeout` across your settings files, capped at 60 seconds.
Set `timeout` on EVERY SessionEnd hook you want extended. Raising the budget via one hook does not extend a sibling hook that has no `timeout` of its own — that one still gets the 1.5s default.

Option B - environment variable: start Claude Code with `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 claude`. This overrides the budget in milliseconds AND becomes the per-hook timeout for every SessionEnd hook that sets no `timeout` of its own (v2.1.268 and later).
If the cleanup genuinely cannot fit in 60 seconds, do not run it inline in a SessionEnd hook. Have the hook spawn a fully detached process and exit immediately.
Do not rely on SessionEnd JSON output to report what happened: Claude Code discards SessionEnd hooks' JSON output fields, including `systemMessage`.

pitfalls.tried: Setting `"timeout": 30` on one SessionEnd hook and assuming all SessionEnd hooks now get 30 seconds.
pitfalls.whyFailed: The highest per-hook `timeout` raises the shared overall budget, but a hook that sets no `timeout` of its own keeps the 1.5-second default and is still cancelled at 1.5s.

pitfalls.tried: Shipping the cleanup hook inside a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` with a generous `timeout`.
pitfalls.whyFailed: "Timeouts set on plugin-provided hooks don't raise the budget." A plugin cannot buy itself more SessionEnd time; the user has to raise the budget from their own settings or via the env var.

pitfalls.tried: Assuming the 600-second default for `command` hooks applies at session end.
pitfalls.whyFailed: SessionEnd overrides it. The 600s default (30s on UserPromptSubmit/PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch, 10s on MessageDisplay) is irrelevant once the event is SessionEnd.

pitfalls.tried: On an older build, setting `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` and expecting a hook with no `timeout` to get the full value.
pitfalls.whyFailed: Before v2.1.268 the env var raised only the overall budget; a hook without its own `timeout` was still cancelled after 1.5 seconds.

pitfalls.tried: Looking for an error in the transcript to confirm the hook ran.
pitfalls.whyFailed: SessionEnd hooks have no decision control and their JSON output fields are discarded, so a cancelled hook leaves no visible signal. Have the script write a timestamped line to a file and check that file instead.

body.verification: Write a SessionEnd hook whose script appends a timestamp to a file, sleeps 3 seconds, then appends a second timestamp. Run a session, then `/clear`. With no `timeout` set, only the first line appears — the hook was cancelled mid-sleep. Re-run with `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 claude` and both lines appear. Use `--debug` to see the hook lifecycle.
body.appliesWhen: Claude Code SessionEnd hooks of any type (command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent), on session exit, `/clear`, or an interactive `/resume` session switch. Verified against docs for Claude Code v2.1.302 (changelog dated 2026-10-16). The env var's "also becomes each hook's default timeout" behavior requires v2.1.268 and later.
body.notAppliesWhen: Other hook events, which keep their own defaults (600s for command/http/mcp_tool, 30s for prompt, 60s for agent, lowered to 30s on UserPromptSubmit/PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch and 10s on MessageDisplay). Before v2.1.268 the env var raised only the shared budget, not the per-hook default. Also does not apply to work you deliberately detach from the hook process, which outlives the budget.
